items.title: Microsoft Entra ID CVSS 10.0 RCE Vulnerability (CVE-2026-69836) Actively Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: A critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-69836) in Microsoft Entra ID holds a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and is confirmed actively exploited in the wild. Unauthenticated attackers can execute arbitrary code on affected identity infrastructure with no user interaction required.
items.why: Entra ID underpins enterprise identity and SSO for millions of orgs. A CVSS 10.0 RCE under active exploitation means full identity infrastructure compromise is possible without credentials. Patch immediately and audit Entra ID logs for anomalous token issuance or admin activity.

items.title: CISA Flags JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 (CVSS 9.8) Auth-Bypass RCE Under Active Exploitation
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-63077 (CVSS 9.8) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — an authentication bypass and RCE flaw in JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD servers. Unauthenticated attackers bypass all auth checks and execute arbitrary OS commands on build servers. Federal agencies face mandatory patch deadline.
items.why: CI/CD pipeline compromise is a premier supply-chain attack vector. An attacker owning a TeamCity server can inject malicious code into software builds, poisoning downstream products. Any internet-facing TeamCity instance must be patched or isolated immediately.

items.title: Palo Alto Unit 42: Iranian APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Multi-Country Espionage with New RAT Variants
items.summary: Unit 42 tracks Screening Serpens (IRGC-affiliated), which has significantly escalated operations since a February 2026 regional conflict. The group deploys two previously undocumented RAT variant families across entities in up to five countries, targeting defense, government, and critical infrastructure.
items.why: State-sponsored Iranian cyber operations have directly escalated with geopolitical tensions. New undocumented RAT families signal active capability development. Defenders — especially orgs with Middle East exposure or defense-sector ties — should hunt the newly published IOCs immediately.

items.title: Strix: Open-Source AI Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework Surpasses 60K GitHub Stars
items.summary: Strix is an open-source AI-driven penetration testing framework that autonomously identifies and helps remediate application vulnerabilities. It reached 60,000 GitHub stars with 1,600 new stars in just 7 days, reflecting explosive adoption in the security research and red team communities.
items.why: AI-driven autonomous offensive tooling is reshaping the attack landscape. Strix lowers the skill bar for attackers and accelerates offensive timelines. Security teams need to understand its capability profile — it will increasingly appear in breach investigations as a first-contact tool.

items.title: Energy & Utilities Hit in 66% of APT Campaigns; Mustang Panda, Lazarus, and Sandworm Simultaneously Active
items.summary: New reporting shows energy and utilities organizations targeted in 66% of observed APT campaigns. Chinese Mustang Panda, North Korean Lazarus, and Russian Sandworm run concurrent operations — FamousSparrow hit an Azerbaijani energy firm; Russia-linked actors struck power infrastructure in Poland and Sweden.
items.why: Three top-tier nation-state actors simultaneously targeting critical infrastructure is a maximum-priority signal. Energy sector attacks risk real-world physical consequences. The cross-regional spread reflects coordinated geopolitical pressure — the entire energy supply chain should treat its threat level as elevated.
